text: That morning: Helen gives her belief that Julia died of fear and shock
why: Helen states this belief in ¶60 during her early-morning visit to Baker Street.

text: How did Julia die? — pure fear and nervous shock
why: Helen says outright that she believes Julia died of pure fear and nervous shock.

text: What frightened Julia in her room?
why: Helen says she cannot imagine what frightened her sister, and the wording does not point at an answer.

text: What frightened Julia in her room? — nothing outside herself: a sudden illness or delusion
id: q.what_frightened=nothing outside herself: a sudden illness or delusion
why: A plain possibility given reason by the story: Julia was alone behind secured door and windows, had no marks or detected poison, and suffered convulsions.
